plan: Given the common knowledge of rationality and a single round, the optimal strategy is to bid slightly above the expected value of the second highest bid. Since values are between $0 and $49, the expected value of the highest of the other two bidders is approximately (2/3) * 49 = ~$32.67. To win, I need to bid higher than that. However, paying too much reduces my profit. I will bid $9.10, slightly above my value, hoping to win against lower values.

Given the common knowledge of rationality, the optimal bidding strategy converges on bidding slightly above the expected value of the second highest bid. Since values are between $0 and $49, a reasonable assumption is that others will bid around half of their value. With my value at $9, I want to win against bids likely below $9/2 = $4.50. Bidding $4.60 secures a win against bids up to $4.50, while minimizing potential overpayment.

Given the common knowledge of rationality, the optimal bidding strategy converges to bidding your true value. This is because any bid below your value risks losing the auction to someone bidding slightly higher, resulting in a missed opportunity to profit. Any bid above your value risks overpaying. Since values are drawn independently each round, past rounds don't directly inform this round's optimal bid. My value is $34, so I will bid $34.
